# Hirobius Design System

Version: 0.34.0

Primary sources: `public/hds-manifest.json`, `src/app/data/component-api.json`, `hirobius.tokens.json`

## Agents Using The Package: Start Here

- Read `AGENTS.md` (package root, `node_modules/@hirobius/design-system/AGENTS.md`) first: which component to use for each screen need, the imports, and the rules.
- MCP server `hds` ships in the package: run `npx hds-mcp` (stdio). Tools: `list_core`, `search_components`, `get_component`, `search_tokens`; each answer is under 2 KB.
- Lint before you finish: `import hds from '@hirobius/design-system/eslint-plugin'` and spread `hds.configs.recommended` into `eslint.config.mjs`.

## Voice

How these docs speak. Every page, and every agent writing for HDS, follows it. Source: `content/docs/voice.mdx` (published at `/docs/voice`).

- Use plain words a reader already knows. Name a thing by what it does, not by how it is built.
- Keep sentences short, one idea each.
- Tell the reader what to do. Leave out brand adjectives.
- Keep maintainer references off public pages: issue and ADR numbers, script names, internal counts.
- Don't use: "systems-first".

## Pick By Need

One answer per need. Use the components after the arrow; what follows "Not:" is what agents reached for instead, which is the wrong answer for that need even where it has a purpose of its own. Generated from `mcp/guide.mjs`, the same list as `AGENTS.md`.

- **Outermost wrapper of a screen** → `Page`, `Stack`. Not: `Container`, `Box`, a bare Stack as the root.
  `<Page><Stack gap="spacious">…one child per section…</Stack></Page>`. `Container` is for a full-bleed surface that is not a page.
  Import: `import { Page } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';` the rest from `@hirobius/design-system`.
- **Screen title with breadcrumb, status and actions** → `PageHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Badge`. Not: Text as the page title, a Stack row of Text and Badge.
  Exactly one per screen: `<PageHeader breadcrumb={<Breadcrumb items={[{ label, href }, { label }]} />} title="…" status={<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>} />`.
  Import: `import { PageHeader } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';` the rest from `@hirobius/design-system`.
- **Row of headline numbers (stats, KPIs, counts, totals)** → `MetricTiles`, `MetricTile`. Not: `Stat`, `StatusTile`, `CardMetric`, Card with Text.
  `<MetricTiles><MetricTile label="Open projects" value="5" />…</MetricTiles>`; one MetricTile per number. `Stat` is for a number inside prose or a dense list, `Card.Metric` for one inside an existing `Card`, a `Card` with `Card.Row` for a state with notes (never a number; it replaces the deprecated `StatusTile`).
  Import: `import { MetricTiles, MetricTile } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';`
- **Table of records with row actions** → `DataTableSection`, `Badge`, `Button`. Not: Table on its own, Card around a Table.
  `<DataTableSection title="Projects" columns={[{ key, label }]} rows={[{ key, cells: [...], actions: <Stack direction="row" gap="tight">…</Stack> }]} />`; leave the actions column out of `columns`.
  Import: `import { DataTableSection } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';` the rest from `@hirobius/design-system`.
- **Switch between panels of related content** → `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`, `TabsContent`. Not: `SegmentedControl`, Button rows.
  `<Tabs defaultValue="a"><TabsList><TabsTrigger value="a">A</TabsTrigger></TabsList><TabsContent value="a">…</TabsContent></Tabs>`.
- **Status label in a header or table cell** → `Badge`. Not: `Tag`, `Text`.
  `<Badge tone="success|info|warning|danger|neutral|inProgress">…</Badge>`; tone is the only styling input.
- **Form with fields and a submit button** → `Form`, `Textarea`, `Input`, `FormActions`, `Button`. Not: a raw `<form>`, a Stack of Buttons as the footer.
  `<Form onSubmit={…}><Textarea label="Notes" … /><FormActions primary={<Button type="submit">Save note</Button>} /></Form>`; every field takes its own `label`.
  Import: `import { Form, FormActions } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';` the rest from `@hirobius/design-system`.
- **Confirm a destructive or irreversible action (delete, archive, remove)** → `AlertDialog`, `Button`. Not: `Dialog`, `window.confirm`.
  Trigger, title, description, Cancel and Action parts: `<AlertDialog><AlertDialog.Trigger asChild><Button …>Archive</Button></AlertDialog.Trigger><AlertDialog.Content><AlertDialog.Header><AlertDialog.Title>…</AlertDialog.Title><AlertDialog.Description>…</AlertDialog.Description></AlertDialog.Header><AlertDialog.Footer><AlertDialog.Cancel asChild><Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button></AlertDialog.Cancel><AlertDialog.Action asChild><Button tone="danger" onClick={…}>Archive</Button></AlertDialog.Action></AlertDialog.Footer></AlertDialog.Content></AlertDialog>`. Focus moves in and returns to the trigger for you.
- **Brief confirmation after an action (saved, archived, sent)** → `ToastProvider`, `useToast`. Not: `Badge`, `Alert`, `Text`.
  Wrap the app root once in `<ToastProvider>`, then `toast({ title: "Note saved", tone: "success" })` from `useToast()`.
- **Message that stays next to its content (error, warning, info)** → `Alert`. Not: Text in a coloured Surface.
  `<Alert tone="warning">…</Alert>`.
- **Button or row action** → `Button`. Not: a raw `<button>`, InlineLink for an action.
  Row actions: `<Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" aria-label="View Brand refresh">View</Button>`; the destructive one adds `tone="danger"`.
- **Space between sections or items** → `Stack`, `Grid`. Not: margins on children, raw px gaps such as px8.
  Stack `gap`: `spacious` between page sections, `normal` inside a section, `tight` between buttons. `Grid` for two-dimensional layout.
- **Padded background or a titled content object** → `Surface`, `Card`. Not: a Box with background and padding.
  `Surface` for a plain padded background; `Card` only when the content has a title or can be pressed.
- **Progress bar or ring** → `Progress`. Not: a hand-built bar.
  `<Progress value={60} label="Upload" />`; inside an existing `Card`, `CardProgress`.
- **Body copy** → `Text`. Not: Text as a section heading.
  Section headings come from the pattern that owns the section (`PageHeader` `title`, `DataTableSection` `title`), not from extra Text.
- **Empty state for a list or section** → `EmptyState`. Not: Text saying "No items".
  `DataTableSection` shows its own through `emptyTitle`; use `EmptyState` elsewhere.
- **The one irreversible action of a screen (delete the client, close the account)** → `DestructiveSection`. Not: a danger Button that acts without a confirm.
  Last on the screen: `<DestructiveSection title="Delete client" description="…" actionLabel="Delete" onConfirm={…} />`; it opens its own AlertDialog. A per-row destructive action uses AlertDialog directly.
  Import: `import { DestructiveSection } from '@hirobius/design-system/patterns';`
- **Read-only details as label and value pairs** → `MetadataList`, `Field`. Not: a Table with two columns, Text pairs in a Stack.
  `<MetadataList items={[{ term: "Owner", description: "Ada" }]} />` for a set; `Field` for one pair.
- **A person, or a group of people** → `Avatar`, `AvatarGroup`. Not: an image in a rounded Box.
  `<Avatar src alt initials />`; several in a row: `<AvatarGroup max={3}>…Avatars…</AvatarGroup>`.
- **A date or time** → `Timestamp`. Not: a formatted string in Text.
  `<Timestamp date="2026-10-14" />` renders a `<time dateTime>`; a date in a table cell may stay plain text.
- **A keyboard key or shortcut hint** → `Kbd`. Not: `InlineCode`, Text in a Box.
  `<Kbd>⌘K</Kbd>`.
- **A quotation with attribution** → `Blockquote`. Not: Callout for a quote, italic Text.
  `<Blockquote attribution="Ada Lovelace">…</Blockquote>`.
- **A fixed-width side rail beside fluid content, or a row that stacks when narrow** → `Sidebar`, `Switcher`. Not: a Grid with media queries.
  `Sidebar` (`side`, `sideWidth`) for rail + content; `Switcher` (`threshold`) for a row that flips to a column. Neither needs a media query.
- **Keep an element stuck while its region scrolls** → `Pin`. Not: position: sticky in style.
  `<Pin top="…">…</Pin>` inside the scrolling region.

## System Architecture

- Engine: React + TypeScript
- Icons: Lucide React
- Tokens: W3C DTCG
- Styling: CSS Variables
- Token pipeline: `hirobius.tokens.json` -> `pnpm tokens` -> generated CSS vars + generated TS constants
- Docs pipeline: `public/hds-manifest.json` + `src/app/data/component-api.json` -> reflective docs pages
- AI entrypoint: read `public/llms.txt` before editing code

## Component Inventory (Source Of Truth)

This file intentionally does not embed the full component list to avoid duplication and excess context.

- Canonical inventory + metadata: read `public/hds-manifest.json`.
- If you see references to `public/manifest.json`, treat it as an optional alias; in this repo prefer `public/hds-manifest.json`.

## Component API (Source Of Truth)

This file intentionally does not embed prop tables or long-form API docs.

- Detailed prop types, unions, defaults, and descriptions: read `src/app/data/component-api.json`.
- Runtime behavior: read the actual component source under `src/app/components/` (and associated styles).

## Core set

The 48 components of the ratified core set: brand-neutral, composable, imported from the package root. Build a screen from these first. Each has `core: true` in `public/hds-manifest.json` and is marked `[core]` under "Which one when". Composed pattern modules (page shells, forms, code blocks, page sections) are imported from `@hirobius/design-system/patterns`.

## Which one when

One line per component that declares when to use it (`@usage` / `@useInstead` in its JSDoc); `[core]` marks the core set. Full detail, including `usage.whenNot`, `keyboard` and `aiRules`, is in `public/hds-manifest.json` and `src/app/data/component-api.json`.

Alert: [core] Show a persistent inline message with a severity, next to the content it concerns. Use instead: ToastProvider, Badge
AlertDialog: Confirm a destructive or irreversible action (delete, archive, remove) before it runs, with Cancel and Action buttons. Use instead: Dialog, ToastProvider
AppShell: The outer frame of a web app: a top bar, a navigation rail or sheet, the page, and an optional detail panel. Use instead: Page, Sidebar
AssetImg: Show an image that scales to its frame, with a placeholder if it fails to load.
AsyncState: Wrap content that loads asynchronously, so it shows skeleton rows while loading, an error with Retry when it fails, your own empty state, and then the content. Use instead: Skeleton, Alert, EmptyState
Avatar: [core] Show a person or entity as an image with an initials fallback, or a neutral person icon when nobody is signed in; add a status dot for a state such as unsynced. As an account button, pass it as the iconLeft of a tertiary iconOnly Button. Use instead: Icon, Badge
Badge: [core] Label a status or state with a compact neutral or semantic chip, a dot, or a capped count beside a heading (`count`, `max`, `label`). Use instead: Tag, Alert
Board: Show work grouped by status as side-by-side columns, each with a title, a count, such as leads by pipeline stage. Use instead: Table, Grid
BoardColumn: Hold the cards for one status inside a Board, with a heading that announces the count. Use instead: Stack
Box: [core] Build one-off layout that no named layout primitive covers, using token keys through `sx`. Use instead: Stack, Grid, Container
Breadcrumb: [core] Show where the current page sits in a hierarchy and link back up it. Use instead: Tabs, Pagination
Button: [core] Run an action, such as submit, save or open a dialog. For an icon-only control pass iconOnly, iconLeft and label; for an on/off toggle pass pressed. For a low-priority action beside a primary one use variant="tertiary" tone="quiet"; for a back link whose icon lines up with the heading add flush; for an action that reads as a text link in a row use variant="link". Use instead: InlineLink
Card: [core] Group related content on a raised surface with header, body, footer and row slots, or as one selectable option. Use instead: Surface
CardFacts: Show an entity's quick facts (location, salary, type) under its title.
CardRow: Show a titled status inside a Card: Card.RowTitle, any Card.RowNote lines, and a Badge in `trailing`.
CardSource: Open an entity card (a job, a lead, a listing) with where it came from and when, above Card.Header.
Checkbox: [core] Let people tick one or more independent options, or a parent choice that is partly selected. Use instead: Toggle, Radio
CodeBlock: Show a code sample with a copy button, optionally collapsed.
Combobox: [core] Pick one value, or several with `multiple`, from a long list of options, with a search field that filters as you type. Use instead: Select, Menu
CommandPalette: [core] Let people jump to a page or run a command from anywhere by typing, opened with ⌘K or Ctrl+K. Use instead: Combobox, Menu
Composer: Capture a prompt or a quick note where a long paste should not flood the field. Use instead: Textarea
Container: [core] Constrain a page region to the content or maximum width and centre it. Use instead: Stack, Grid, Box
DataTableSection: Put a heading and toolbar above a Table.
DestructiveSection: Put a dangerous action, such as delete, in its own section with a warning and a confirm step.
Dialog: [core] Interrupt the page with a modal that needs a decision or focused input before people continue. Use instead: Tooltip, Alert, ToastProvider, AlertDialog
Disclosure: [core] Hide optional explanatory content behind a heading that people can expand. An expandable list row (one-line preview, actions beside the trigger) is variant="row". Use instead: Tabs
Divider: [core] Separate two blocks of content with a thin line. Use instead: Stack, Surface
EmptyState: [core] Say that a list, grid or section has no data yet, with a title, an optional description, and an optional action that teaches the next step. When the empty state is the whole view and teaches the first step, use variant="teaching" (centred, icon tile, bold title); add framed when it sits loose on the page. Use instead: Skeleton, Alert
ErrorPattern: Show an error with a short message and a Back button, in place or as a full page.
Field: [core] Show a labelled read-only value, such as a name and its value in a detail view. Use instead: Input
Form: Wrap form fields so they stack with even spacing.
FormActions: Lay out a form's buttons in a fixed order: danger on the left, then secondary, then primary on the right.
Grid: [core] Lay out content in columns that adapt to the screen width, or line up nested content with subgrid. Use instead: Stack, Box
HdsRouterProvider: [core] Wrap the app root once so HDS links and navigation use your client router; with no provider they stay plain anchors.
HdsThemeProvider: [core] Wrap an app or region once to set theme, density and other root attributes for everything inside it. Use instead: Surface
Icon: [core] Show a Lucide icon at a set size and color. Use instead: Button, Avatar
InlineLink: [core] Link to a route or external URL from inside body copy. Use instead: Button, Text
Input: [core] Collect a single line of text, a number, an email, a password, a date or a time, with label, helper and error slots. Use instead: Textarea, Select, Combobox
Kbd: [core] Show a keyboard key or shortcut hint inline, as a native kbd element. Use instead: Text
List: [core] Show groups of records (roles, documents, settings) as rows with a leading tile, a title, one description line, one meta line and one quiet trailing affordance; the whole row opens the record. Use instead: NavList, MetadataList, Table
ListEmpty: Say that a List.Group has no rows yet, in place of its items. Use instead: NavList, MetadataList, Table
ListGroup: One titled group of List.Item rows, with a count Badge and an optional action in its heading. Use instead: NavList, MetadataList, Table
ListItem: One record in a List.Group: a title, a description, a meta line and one trailing affordance, the whole row tappable. Use instead: NavList, MetadataList, Table
ListTile: Put an icon in a sunken square at the start of a List.Item (its `leading`). Use instead: NavList, MetadataList, Table
Menu: [core] Offer a list of actions from a trigger, closed until opened. Use instead: Select
MetaLine: [core] Show one or two secondary facts on a single line, joined by a bullet ("Acme Cloud · Remote"). Use instead: A
NavList: [core] List sibling destinations as rows that can hold a title, a meta line and a badge, with the open one marked current (a rail of jobs, documents or records). Use instead: Tabs, Breadcrumb, Menu
NavListItem: List sibling destinations as rows that can hold a title, a meta line and a badge, with the open one marked current (a rail of jobs, documents or records). Use instead: Tabs, Breadcrumb, Menu
Page: Wrap a screen in the standard width and padding.
PageHeader: Open a screen with its title, plus optional breadcrumb, status and actions.
Pagination: [core] Move between pages of a long result set, with truncated page numbers. Use instead: Breadcrumb
Popover: [core] Anchor interactive content, such as a short form, a filter set or a picker, to a trigger people click to open. Use instead: Tooltip, Menu, Dialog
Progress: [core] Show how far a task has got, as a bar or ring that is determinate or indeterminate. Use instead: Spinner, Skeleton
Radio: [core] Choose exactly one option from a small set that should stay visible together. Use instead: Checkbox, Select, SegmentedControl
Reveal: Fade content in as it scrolls into view.
SegmentedControl: [core] Switch between two to five mutually exclusive views or modes in a compact row. Use instead: Radio, Tabs, Select
Select: [core] Choose one value from a short list of options in a form field. Use instead: Menu, Combobox
Sheet: Open a short menu or form from the bottom edge on a phone (sort, row actions, status, a quick edit), centred like a Dialog on wider screens. Use instead: Dialog, AlertDialog, Menu
Skeleton: [core] Reserve the shape of content that is still loading, so the layout does not jump. Use instead: Progress, Spinner
Slider: [core] Pick a number within a known range by dragging, when the exact value matters less than the position. Use instead: Input
Spinner: [core] Show that something is loading when the wait is short or has no measurable end. Use instead: Progress, Skeleton
Stack: [core] Space items in a row or column with even gaps. Use instead: Grid, Surface
Surface: [core] Give a block of content a background and padding, with no header or footer. Use instead: Card, Stack
Table: [core] Show rows of structured data in aligned columns, with optional sorting. Use instead: Field, Stack
Tabs: [core] Switch between panels of related content in the same place, one visible at a time. Use instead: SegmentedControl, Disclosure
Tag: [core] Show an interactive filter or category chip that people can toggle. Use instead: Badge
Text: [core] Set any text on the type ramp, with the element chosen by `as`. Use instead: InlineLink, Kbd
Textarea: [core] Collect multi-line free text such as a message, note or description. Use instead: Input
ThemeToggle: A single header or menu control to switch between the light and dark theme. Use instead: SegmentedControl
Timeline: [core] Show a dated history of events, such as shipped releases or client activity, grouped under day headings. Use instead: MetadataList, StatusListItem
ToastProvider: [core] Confirm an action with a brief message that appears and dismisses itself, through useToast. Use instead: Alert, Dialog
Toggle: [core] Switch one setting on or off, with the effect applying immediately. Use instead: Checkbox, Radio
TokenField: Edit a template or message in which placeholders such as [Name] must stay whole: each one is a chip that is stepped over and deleted as one unit. Use instead: Textarea, Input
Tooltip: [core] Name an icon-only control, or add a short hint that appears on hover and keyboard focus. Use instead: Popover, Text
VisuallyHidden: [core] Give assistive technology a label or description that sighted people do not need to see. Use instead: Text

## Tokens (Primary Source Of Truth)

- Primary token source of truth: `hirobius.tokens.json` (W3C DTCG).
- Prefer `semantic.*` and `component.*` tokens for product UI. Use `primitive.*` only when editing the token system itself.
- CSS variable naming convention: token path `semantic.color.surface.page` maps to `var(--semantic-color-surface-page)`.

## Quick Token Reference

| Need | Token path examples | CSS var examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page/background surfaces | `semantic.color.surface.page`, `semantic.color.surface.raised` | `--semantic-color-surface-page`, `--semantic-color-surface-raised` |
| Text/content colors | `semantic.color.content.primary`, `semantic.color.content.secondary` | `--semantic-color-content-primary`, `--semantic-color-content-secondary` |
| Borders/dividers | `semantic.color.border.default`, `semantic.color.border.interactive` | `--semantic-color-border-default`, `--semantic-color-border-interactive` |
| Feedback states | `semantic.color.feedback.error`, `semantic.color.feedback.success` | `--semantic-color-feedback-error`, `--semantic-color-feedback-success` |
| Spacing (semantic tiers) | `semantic.space.scale.2xs`, `semantic.space.fixed.2xs`, `semantic.space.surface.padding` | use semantic tokens or `--hds-space-px12` style vars |
| Radius | `semantic.radius.action` | `--semantic-radius-action` |
| Motion | `semantic.motion.productive`, `semantic.motion.expressive`, `semantic.motion.exit` | use token refs; values are structured (duration/easing) |
| Typography | `semantic.typography.body`, `semantic.typography.title`, `semantic.typography.caption` | use token refs; values are structured (family/size/weight/etc) |

## How To Lay Out A Screen

Canonical skeleton, outermost to innermost:

1. `Page` (from `@hirobius/design-system/patterns`; or `Container` for a full-bleed, non-page surface, with a `Box` inside it for a horizontal gutter) for the outermost width constraint. Never import `Container` directly inside `src/app/pages/**` — use `Page`, which wraps it and owns vertical rhythm.
2. `Stack` (vertical rhythm between sections) or `Grid` (two-dimensional/column layout) for the structural skeleton. One section = one Section/Stack — never add a second wrapper to fake a section boundary.
3. Reach for a named layout primitive before hand-rolling flex/grid math for a common intent: `Stack direction="row" wrap="wrap"` (wrapping row of same-ish things), `Sidebar` (fixed-width rail + fluid content, no media query), `Switcher` (row that flips to a column below a threshold, no media query). A full-height shell with a centered main region, an aspect-ratio-locked media box or a negative margin that escapes a parent padding is a `Box` with `style` (not `sx`, which applies on the client only).
4. `Surface` for any background-bearing, padded wrapper (card, panel, inset). Never a raw element with backgroundColor + padding hand-rolled inline.
5. Use the screen patterns (`@hirobius/design-system/patterns`) for the parts every screen repeats: `PageHeader` once at the top (breadcrumb, `heading2` title, status, actions), `MetricTiles` for any row of headline numbers, `FormActions` for a form footer (primary right-most and last in DOM order, destructive on the far left), `DataTableSection` for a titled table (toolbar slot, consumer row actions, empty state, scrolls on narrow widths without a caller `minWidth`), and `DestructiveSection` last for an irreversible action (danger button, then an `AlertDialog` confirm). A row of headline numbers is always `MetricTiles`; `Stat`, `Card.Metric` and `StatusTile` answer other needs (see "Pick By Need" in `llms.txt`). Pick between `Card` and `Surface` with the "Which one, when" table in `DESIGN.md`.
6. `Box` with `style` (or `sx`) is used last, only for genuinely one-off layout that no named primitive covers (prefer `style` over `sx`, as `sx` applies on the client only). `sx` spacing/color keys must be HDS token keys, never raw hex or px.

Negative rules (apply everywhere, checked by `scripts/audit-tokens.mjs --full`, `check-hardcoded-spacing.mjs`, `check-hardcoded-colors.mjs`):

- No inline margins on children to fake spacing between siblings — gap/spacing on the parent (Stack/Grid/Switcher/Sidebar) owns rhythm, not margin on the child.
- No raw px or hex values in any layout or color prop — every spacing value comes from the semantic gap scale (`tight | normal | inset | spacious`, or a component/subgrid step) and every color comes from a `semantic.color.*` token.
- No repeated outlined cards as the default structure for roadmap/status/process/overview UI — use open bands, dividers, rails, disclosures, and whitespace instead.
- No primitive spacing: never a `primitive.space.*` step, `--primitive-space-*` var, `hds.space.px*` or numeric Tailwind spacing class (`p-4`, `gap-2`) — use `semantic.space.*` (`p-surface-padding`, `gap-scale-md`, `var(--semantic-space-scale-*)`) or the `xs…xl` keys. `hds/no-primitive-spacing` enforces it.
- Spacing rhythm: inner padding ≤ outer gap; a nested surface steps down one level (surface.padding → `sm` → `xs`) or takes `padding="none"`; sibling cards share one padding.

Density: the default rhythm is roomy, for sites. Dense apps put `data-density="compact"` on the same `[data-hds]` scope element (or `<html>`): `semantic.space.scale` sm/md/lg/xl become 12/16/24/32px, `section.stack` 48px, and type body 15 · ui 14 · caption 13 · title 24px (display stays 56px). Surface padding, region gutter and grid gap follow the scale; `Table` follows it unless given a `density` prop.

Reference: `docs/architecture/variant-contract.md` for structural/semantic/size/density variance; `src/app/data/component-api.json` for every layout primitive's full prop table and `@ai-rules` guidance.

## How To Build A Scroll-Driven Section

Canonical primitives, cheapest-first (CSS before JS, JS before an opt-in dependency):

1. `Reveal` (CSS `animation-timeline: view()`) for fade/slide/scale-in-on-enter — zero JS, zero deps. Pick `animation` from `fade | fade-up | fade-down | scale`. Content is visible by DEFAULT; the effect applies only where `animation-timeline` is supported and the user has not requested reduced motion — never gate visibility behind either.
2. `Pin` (`position: sticky`) for a pinned scroll scene — the dependency-free basis for the "tall section + sticky child" pattern (GSAP's `pin: true`, done with zero JS). Give the pinned element a TALLER scrolling parent (e.g. `height: 300vh`) so it has room to travel; `top` is a CSS length offset, not a spacing token.
3. `useScrollProgress` (from `@hirobius/design-system/scroll`) only when the 0→1 scroll value is needed in React — cross-element choreography, canvas/WebGL, or a Motion (`motion/react`) `useTransform` binding that CSS `animation-timeline` cannot express. Thin, SSR-guarded wrapper over Motion `useScroll`; adds no new dependency.
4. `SmoothScroll` (from `@hirobius/design-system/scroll`, `lenis` as an OPTIONAL peer dep) only for opt-in momentum ("inertia") scrolling, mounted once at the app/site root. Never imported from the main barrel — consumers who skip it pay nothing. Reduced-motion-first: Lenis is not instantiated when the user prefers reduced motion, unless `ignoreReducedMotion` is set for a deliberate art-directed exception.
5. Do not adopt GSAP/ScrollTrigger, and do not wire Lenis directly outside `SmoothScroll`, inside the core library — the CSS + Motion stack above covers reveal/pin/scrub without new dependencies. Bespoke GSAP/Lenis/WebGL scenes stay app-level/downstream (marketing sites, the clients factory), composed from these primitives.

Negative rules:

- No hand-rolled IntersectionObserver reveal-on-scroll logic — use `Reveal`.
- No hand-rolled `position: sticky` scroll scenes — use `Pin`.
- No GSAP/ScrollTrigger or bespoke Lenis wiring inside `@hirobius/design-system` — those stay app-level/downstream, composed from `Reveal`/`Pin`/`useScrollProgress`/`SmoothScroll`.
- Every scroll effect must degrade to fully visible/static content — never gate content visibility behind `animation-timeline` support or a scroll listener with no fallback.

Reference: `src/app/components/reveal.tsx`, `src/app/components/pin.tsx`, `src/scroll/` (`use-scroll-progress.ts`, `smooth-scroll.tsx`), and the Reveal pattern page on the docs site (`/docs/patterns/reveal`) for golden-path examples.

## HDS Card Anatomy (mandatory — every property is non-negotiable)

When building any card component or card-like surface, ALL of the following rules apply. There is no creative latitude here — deviation from any property is a bug.

| Property | Required value | Forbidden |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `var(--semantic-color-surface-raised)` | Custom colors, gradients, tinted fills, any non-token value |
| Border | `1px solid var(--semantic-color-border-default)` | `box-shadow` as an elevation substitute |
| Border radius | `rounded-lg` (`role.radius` + 4 px: 12 px by default, follows the tenant) | `var(--component-card-radius)`, `rounded-full`, or any hard-coded value |
| Padding | `var(--semantic-space-surface-padding)` or `<Surface padding="component">` | Raw pixel values, Tailwind spacing classes, ad hoc insets |
| Shadow | Resting cards: none (`elevation.flat`). Interactive lifted state: `shadow.subtle` via `elevation.raised`. Never reach for shadow values directly — bind via `var(--semantic-elevation-{role}-shadow)` | Raw `box-shadow` values, `drop-shadow`, glow, or any depth effect not bound to a role token |
| Title | `hds.typeStyles.heading3` / `<Text variant="heading3">` | Any other type style for the primary card heading |
| Subtitle / meta | `hds.typeStyles.caption` / `<Text variant="caption">` + `var(--semantic-color-content-secondary)` | Primary color, body size, or custom color for secondary text |
| Hover (interactive cards only) | `transform: scale(1.02)` CSS transform | Background color change, fill swap, border color shift on hover |

**NEVER on any card surface:** gradient backgrounds, glow effects, frosted glass (`backdrop-filter: blur`), decorative overlays, gradient borders, colored or tinted card backgrounds, inner shadows, patterned backgrounds, AI-aesthetic shimmer or particle effects. Never reach for shadow values directly — bind to a `semantic.elevation.*` role bundle so surface + shadow + border stay coherent.

## Elevation roles

| Surface | Role token | Background | Shadow | Border |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Card / panel resting | `semantic.elevation.flat` | `surface.page` | none | `border.subtle` 1px |
| Card / panel lifted (interactive only) | `semantic.elevation.raised` | `surface.raised` | `shadow.subtle` | none |
| Tooltip | `semantic.elevation.floating` | `surface.inverse` | `shadow.floating` | none |
| Menu / popover / listbox / toast / dialog | `semantic.elevation.overlay` | `surface.floating` | `shadow.overlay` | `border.default` 1px |

Cards default to `elevation.flat`. Tooltips use `elevation.floating`. Menus, popovers, listboxes, toasts and dialogs use `elevation.overlay`. Interactive cards lift to `elevation.raised` on hover. Never combine `raised` with a border — depth is one mechanism (border OR shadow), not both stacked.

Overlays (Dialog, AlertDialog, Menu, Popover, Select, Tooltip) portal into the nearest `data-hds` scope, so they inherit its theme (for example `<div data-hds data-theme="dark">`); pass `container` on the Content part to override.

Paths in this file that begin with `docs/architecture/`, `src/app/components/`, `src/scroll/` or under `scripts/`, or that name `public/manifest.json`, `DESIGN-HANDOFF.md` or `TOKEN_GOVERNANCE.md` exist only in the source repo, not in the npm package. Everything under "Default context" below ships in the package.

## Icons

Icons come from the curated subpath `@hirobius/design-system/icons`; nothing extra to install.

```tsx
import { Button, Icon } from '@hirobius/design-system';
import { Ellipsis } from '@hirobius/design-system/icons';

<Button iconOnly label="Row actions" iconLeft={<Icon icon={Ellipsis} />} />
```

Rule: icon-only actions (row menus, close, edit) use `Button iconOnly` with a `label` and an `Icon` in `iconLeft`; do not hand-roll a button with a glyph or text "...".

Names: Archive, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowUpRight, Banknote, Bell, Bookmark, Briefcase, Calendar, Check, ChevronDown, ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, ChevronUp, CircleAlert, CircleCheck, CircleHelp, Clock, Copy, Download, Ellipsis, EllipsisVertical, ExternalLink, Eye, EyeOff, FileText, Funnel, Heart, House, Image, Images, Info, Link, Lock, LogIn, LogOut, Mail, MapPin, Menu, Minus, Pencil, Phone, Plus, RefreshCw, Save, Search, Settings, Share, Star, Trash2, TriangleAlert, Upload, User, Users, Wrench, X

Legacy names map to canonical ones: MoreHorizontal -> Ellipsis, MoreVertical -> EllipsisVertical, AlertTriangle -> TriangleAlert, Home -> House, Filter -> Funnel.

Name collisions: `Menu` shares a name with an HDS component; alias the icon: `import { Menu as MenuIcon } from '@hirobius/design-system/icons'`. For an icon outside the set, install `lucide-react@0.487.0` (same version keeps the `LucideIcon` type identical).

## Token Rules

- Component inventory: read `public/hds-manifest.json`. Do not duplicate inventories in markdown.
- Component prop API: read `src/app/data/component-api.json`. Do not inline prop tables in `llms.txt`.
- Token source of truth: read `hirobius.tokens.json` (W3C DTCG). Prefer `semantic.*` and `component.*` tokens over `primitive.*` for product UI.
- CSS variables: token path `semantic.color.surface.page` maps to `var(--semantic-color-surface-page)` (see generated token refs).
- Docs: use `DESIGN.md` as the default lean visual spec. Load `DESIGN-HANDOFF.md` only on-demand.
- Load `TOKEN_GOVERNANCE.md` only on-demand (when explicitly requested or required by the task).
- Never transform text to uppercase; sentence case for all UI text, including eyebrows, pre-titles, labels, captions and table headers. Raw content keeps its own case (an acronym, a user's string). Enforced by `scripts/check-no-uppercase.mjs`.
- Accent: graphite by default; `data-accent="cobalt"` on `<html>` swaps the accent tokens to cobalt.
- Read `public/llms.txt` before touching code so AI workflows start from the same system map as humans.

## Agent Workflow

1. Read `public/llms.txt` and the relevant source files.
2. Check `public/hds-manifest.json` for component metadata and phase status.
3. Check `src/app/data/component-api.json` for prop names, unions, defaults, and descriptions.
4. Use `hirobius.tokens.json` (and generated CSS vars) for styling decisions, never raw hex or ad hoc values.
5. Run `pnpm tokens:audit` or `pnpm build` after changes that affect docs, tokens, or manifests.

## Upgrading

This text describes @hirobius/design-system 0.34.0. To move a project to the newest release, run `npx @hirobius/design-system@latest upgrade` from its root: it runs the codemods, bumps the dependency, installs, typechecks, and lists what is left to do by hand. `npx @hirobius/design-system@latest upgrade --check` changes nothing and exits 1 while work is left. It also refreshes the `hds-consumer` skill when the project has a `.claude/skills/` folder. The full guide is `UPGRADING.md`; the machine-readable record is `upgrade/index.json`.

Every name a release removed, moved or renamed, and what to use instead:

| Old name | Use instead | Release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Hds-prefix` | Twelve component families, such as HdsAlertDialog and HdsDateInput, lost their Hds prefix before any release shipped them, so import each by its bare name (AlertDialog, DateInput). | 0.12.0 |
| `InfoPage` | InfoPage and InfoPageProps are removed with no replacement; it was portfolio scaffolding, so delete the code that uses it. | 0.12.0 |
| `StatTone-FieldTone` | StatProps["tone"] and FieldProps["tone"] | 0.12.0 |
| `primitive-typography-tokens` | Six unused typography tokens are removed (--primitive-typography-size-2xs, -weight-light, -weight-semibold, -letterSpacing-tighter, -wide and -wider); replace a var() that reads one with your own value. | 0.16.0 |

## Deprecated: do not use in new code

Still exported, but on the way out: do not write new code with them.

- `hds` (removed in 0.35.0): Importing hds from the package root still works but is deprecated; import it from @hirobius/design-system/tokens instead.
- `tokens` (removed in 0.35.0): Importing tokens from the package root still works but is deprecated; import it from @hirobius/design-system/tokens instead.
- `Blockquote.size` (removed in 1.0.0): Blockquote has one size (md); the size prop, including sm and lg, still renders as before until removed.
- `Box-sx-layout-names` (removed in 1.0.0): Box sx spacing names 'tight', 'normal', 'inset' and 'spacious' still work but are deprecated, and a development build warns once for each; use 'sm' to 'xl' instead.
- `CardMetric` (removed in 1.0.0): Card.Metric is deprecated and still works; no replacement is planned, so compose a Card with the type roles (caption label, display or title value).
- `Divider.strong` (removed in 1.0.0): Divider's strong prop, deprecated since before 0.16.0, still works; use variant="strong" instead.
- `InlineCode.compact` (removed in 1.0.0): InlineCode's compact prop, deprecated since before 0.16.0, still works; use density="compact" instead.
- `MetricTile` (removed in 1.0.0): MetricTile is deprecated and still works; no replacement is planned, so compose a Card with the type roles (caption label, display or title value).
- `MetricTiles` (removed in 1.0.0): MetricTiles is deprecated and still works; no replacement is planned, so compose a Card with the type roles (caption label, display or title value).
- `Stack-gap-layout-names` (removed in 1.0.0): Stack gap names 'tight', 'normal', 'inset' and 'spacious' still work and do not warn yet, but are removed in 1.0.0, and Stack names no replacement until then.
- `Stat` (removed in 1.0.0): Stat is deprecated and still works; no replacement is planned, so compose a Card with the type roles (caption label, display or title value).
- `StatusTile` (removed in 1.0.0): StatusTile still works until 1.0.0; replace it with <Card padding="item" className="border-0"><Card.Row trailing={trailing}><Card.RowTitle>{title}</Card.RowTitle> plus one <Card.RowNote> per note, and drop tone, which StatusTile never painted.
- `Text-variants` (removed in 1.0.0): The Text variants heading1, heading2, heading3, technical, eyebrow, badge, docLede, docBody, docSmall and docCode still work but are deprecated; use title, mono, caption, body or ui instead.
- `hds.density` (removed in 1.0.0): hds.density still works but is deprecated; use hds.semantic.space.scale one step down, so density.sm becomes scale.xs.
- `hds.density` (removed in 1.0.0): hds.density is deprecated; the upgrade command rewrites hds.density.sm to hds.semantic.space.scale.xs (md to sm, lg to md, xl to lg, xl2 to xl), the same pixels. density.xs, xl3 and xl4 have no scale step: use hds.space.px4, px64 or px80, which do not shrink under compact density.
- `max-w-2xl`, `pt-1`, `sm:text-4xl` (removed in 1.0.0): Sixteen Tailwind utilities that only HDS's deleted internal files used, such as pt-1 and max-w-2xl, still ship in styles.css and tokens.css until 1.0.0, so a page that relies on HDS's compiled CSS for them should generate them with its own Tailwind.
- `typeStyles-aliases` (removed in 1.0.0): The hds.typeStyles keys from before the ramp (h1 to h3, heading1 to heading3, eyebrow, badge, micro, technical, small, label and the rest) and hds.semantic.typography label, labelDescriptive and labelTechnical still work but are deprecated; use display, title, body, ui, caption or mono instead.

Deprecated design tokens are not listed: the `hds/no-deprecated-token` lint rule flags each use and names its replacement.

## Key Files

- `public/hds-manifest.json` - canonical machine-readable system inventory, metadata, and token snapshot
- `src/app/data/component-api.json` - generated prop reference (source of truth for prop docs)
- `hirobius.tokens.json` - token source of truth (W3C DTCG)
- `public/llms.txt` - machine-readable AI context index
- `DESIGN.md` - lean agent-facing visual spec (default)
- `DESIGN-HANDOFF.md` - verbose visual language mirror (on-demand only)

# DESIGN.md (full)

<!-- GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT. Source: DESIGN.source.md. Regenerate with `pnpm tokens`. -->

# DESIGN.md

A machine- and human-readable specification of the Hirobius Design System for AI agents, design tools, and humans generating or reviewing UI. Values are sourced from `hirobius.tokens.json`; narrative rules are hand-authored. For the full tokens reference see `DESIGN-HANDOFF.md`.

## Overview

Hirobius is a clean, structured visual language that bridges digital precision and physical fabrication through a high-contrast near-monochrome neutral palette tinted toward midnight (OKLCH hue 262) and a single accent that each direction or brand sets (ADR-035) — a midnight graphite by default. Its personality is disciplined, tactile, and quietly technical: structure is explicit, motion is purposeful, and visual noise is stripped away. Whitespace is treated as material, not leftover space, so every screen should feel deliberate, breathable, and exact.

## Colors

<!-- auto:start:colors -->
**One accent — one neutral system.**

- **Accent** (`#0F1726`, graphite): CTAs, active states, selected focus rings, and the single brand accent. `semantic.accent.rest` — a lever each direction or brand sets, not a fixed hue (ADR-035) (#208).
- **Accent theme — Cobalt** (`#112DE8`): opt-in swap of the accent tokens only. Set `data-accent="cobalt"` on `<html>` (source `accents/cobalt/tokens.json`); graphite stays the default. Still one accent per screen.
- **Neutral**: backgrounds, surfaces, borders, text. True monochromatic — `primitive.color.neutral.50` through `950`. Use `semantic.color.surface.*`, `semantic.color.content.*`, `semantic.color.border.*`; never reach directly for primitives in components.
- **Feedback — Error** (`#B91C1C`): destructive confirms, error banners, validation failures. `semantic.color.feedback.error`.
- **Feedback — Success** (`#047857`): positive confirmations, completed states. `semantic.color.feedback.success`.
- **Feedback — Warning** (`#92400E`): cautions, recoverable issues. `semantic.color.feedback.warning`.
- **Feedback — Info** (`#1E2EFD`): neutral announcements and inline guidance. `semantic.color.feedback.info`.

Feedback hues are never decorative; do not use them as accents. Light and dark mode values are defined per-token in `hirobius.tokens.json`.
<!-- auto:end:colors -->

## Typography

<!-- auto:start:typography -->
HDS ships three typefaces — each with a distinct role:

- **Display / Heading font**: Sora. Bound to the `display` and `title` styles.
- **Body / UI font**: Plus Jakarta Sans. All prose, labels, small text, captions, and UI copy.
- **Mono font**: IBM Plex Mono. Reserved for tokens, code, technical callouts, and metric readouts.

Weights declared: `400` regular, `400` mono, `500` medium, `600` semibold, `700` bold, `700` display. Heading styles (display · title) use `700` display; body, UI, and caption use `400` regular / `500` medium; mono uses `400` mono. Declared but unused by any semantic role: `600` semibold, `700` bold.

### Type ramp

| Role | Size (desktop max) | Compact | Weight | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `semantic.typography.hero` | 120px | same | 700 | Marketing-only extension above the ramp (ADR-052 addendum): covers and marketing headers, never product UI |
| `semantic.typography.display` | 56px | same | 700 | One per page, hero only |
| `semantic.typography.title` | 28px | 24px | 700 | Section and card headings |
| `semantic.typography.titleSm` | 20px | same | 700 | Small heading inside a card or section band, and the Alert title |
| `semantic.typography.body` | 18px | 15px | 400 | Prose |
| `semantic.typography.bodyStrong` | 18px | 15px | 700 | Variant of body: weight 700, what Text with weight bold renders |
| `semantic.typography.ui` | 16px | 14px | 500 | Controls, nav, table text, values |
| `semantic.typography.uiRegular` | 16px | 14px | 400 | Variant of ui: weight 400, for table body cells and other plain UI text |
| `semantic.typography.uiItalic` | 16px | 14px | 500 | Variant of ui: italic, what the inline EmptyState message renders |
| `semantic.typography.caption` | 14px | 13px | 500 | Metadata, help text and labels, in sentence case |
| `semantic.typography.mono` | 15px | same | 400 | Code and ids, 15px / 1.5 / 400 |
| `semantic.typography.lineHeight.none` |  | same |  | Semantic alias for leading-none (1) |

> The ramp is static: tokens store the value every surface renders. **Compact** is the size under `data-density="compact"` (dense apps). Deprecated roles are left out of this table; `hds/no-deprecated-token` names their replacement.
<!-- auto:end:typography -->

**Never for.** Each role has one job; reaching past it is how the ramp drifts.

- `display`: never for a section heading, a card or anything twice on a page. It is the hero line only.
- `title`: never for body copy or a label, and never skip a level to make a heading smaller; use `titleSm` for a heading inside a card or band.
- `titleSm`: never for page-level headings, and never for emphasis inside prose (bold the words instead).
- `body`: never for controls, table cells or metadata (those are `ui` and `caption`). A lead paragraph is `body` plus a quieter colour, not a bigger size.
- `ui`: never for long prose, and never for a heading. It is the size of things you act on or scan.
- `caption`: never for the only copy a user needs to act on, never uppercase, and never below the `caption` size to fit more in.
- `mono`: never for ordinary emphasis or for whole paragraphs. Code, ids and metric readouts only.

**Casing.** Never transform text to uppercase; sentence case for all UI text, including eyebrows, pre-titles, labels, captions and table headers. Raw content keeps its own case (an acronym, a user's string). No `text-transform: uppercase`, Tailwind `uppercase`, `textCase: UPPER` or `.toUpperCase()` for display; `scripts/check-no-uppercase.mjs` fails the commit. Tracking never exists to support caps.

**Meta lines.** A bullet-separated line holds at most two text items ("Acme Cloud · Remote"), because long translated strings wrap mid-line. More facts get one row each. Use `MetaLine` (`items` is a one- or two-item tuple, a third is a type error); `hds/max-two-meta-items` flags hand-rolled `A · B · C` chains.

## Spacing

<!-- auto:start:spacing -->
**Base unit: 4px.** All spacing snaps to the primitive scale; never introduce half-steps or arbitrary px values.

Scale: `0px` (`primitive.space.0`) · `1px` (`primitive.space.px1`) · `2px` (`primitive.space.px2`) · `4px` (`primitive.space.1`) · `6px` (`primitive.space.px6`) · `8px` (`primitive.space.2`) · `10px` (`primitive.space.px10`) · `12px` (`primitive.space.3`) · `16px` (`primitive.space.4`) · `20px` (`primitive.space.5`) · `24px` (`primitive.space.6`) · `28px` (`primitive.space.7`) · `32px` (`primitive.space.8`) · `40px` (`primitive.space.10`) · `48px` (`primitive.space.12`) · `64px` (`primitive.space.16`) · `80px` (`primitive.space.20`) · `96px` (`primitive.space.24`) · `128px` (`primitive.space.32`)

Semantic scale (comfortable, the default): `2xs` 4px · `xs` 8px · `sm` 20px · `md` 28px · `lg` 40px · `xl` 64px.

Compact (`data-density="compact"`, for dense apps): `2xs` 4px · `xs` 8px · `sm` 12px · `md` 16px · `lg` 24px · `xl` 32px.

Fixed steps between the rungs (density does not move them): `fixed.2xs` 4px · `fixed.xs` 12px · `fixed.sm` 16px · `fixed.md` 24px · `fixed.lg` 32px · `fixed.xl` 48px. Every spacing value has a semantic token; never type a px value.

Layout rhythm, padding, and gaps use the `semantic.space.scale.{xs…xl}` steps (and `none`), never a raw `primitive.space.*` value or a numeric Tailwind class; `primitive.space.*` is the ramp behind the scale. Use `semantic.space.*` aliases (e.g. `semantic.space.surface.padding`) when the purpose is established. `data-density="compact"` (on `<html>` or the `[data-hds]` scope element) is the one opt-in tighter mode: it remaps `semantic.space.scale.sm…xl` to the app rhythm above (`2xs` and `xs` stay 4px and 8px), the deprecated `layout.*` steps and `section.stack` (48px) with it, and sets the compact type sizes in the ramp table; `semantic.space.surface.padding`, `semantic.space.region.gutter` and `Table` follow it. The `--hds-space-{xs…4xl}` vars are a legacy bridge that no component reads.
<!-- auto:end:spacing -->

**Spacing rules of thumb** (2026-10, raised with the type ramp so padding, gaps and line height stay in rhythm):

- **Inner padding ≤ outer gap.** A surface's padding is never larger than the gap around it: a 28px card sits in a grid gap of 28px or more, never 20px.
- **Nested surfaces step down one level.** A surface inside a surface takes the next smaller step (surface.padding → `sm` → `xs`), or `padding="none"`.
- **Never mix two paddings on sibling cards.** Cards in one row or list share one padding step.
- **Semantic tokens only.** Components and consumers use `semantic.space.*` (or the `xs…xl` keys); never a `primitive.space.*` step, a numeric Tailwind class or raw px. `hds/no-primitive-spacing` (in `hds/recommended`) and `check-tailwind-spacing-scale --ratchet` (pretest) fail on them.

## Layout contract (v1)

Approved 2026-10-07 as the **target**; adoption is in progress, so some components below (Container, Sidebar, Switcher) still ship until they fold in. Data: `docs/guardrails/layout-contract.json`; gates: `pnpm check:layout-contract` (warn mode; baseline in `docs/audits/layout-contract-baseline.md`) and `check-tailwind-spacing-scale --ratchet` (pretest; per-file baseline in `scripts/tailwind-spacing-scale.baseline.json`).

1. **Sizing.** Every component declares `fill` or `hug` on each axis. Leaves hug. Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, Table, Progress and Divider fill width. One override prop, `width="hug|fill"`, on every component. Height always hugs; stretching is the parent's job (`align="stretch"`). No component sets `h-full`, `height: 100%` or `self-*` on its root.
2. **Padding.** Only containers pad: Card, Surface, Alert, Callout, Dialog, Page. Compound parts (`Card.Header`, `Body`, `Footer`, `Metric`) have zero padding and the container's `gap` spaces them. Padding is `none | sm | md`, default `md`, density-aware. A padded container directly inside a padded container is an error unless the inner one is `padding="none"`.
3. **Spacing.** One scale, `xs…xl` (plus `none`), for every `gap` and `padding` prop. Every gap defaults to `md`. No outer margins on any component; space between siblings is the parent's `gap`.
4. **Primitives.** Stack, Grid, Page (absorbs Container) and Surface compose layouts. Box and Pin are escape hatches. Sidebar and Switcher fold into Stack and Grid.
5. **Forms.** A form control in a form context has a max width (`40rem` by default) and siblings share one width.

## Corner-Radius Policy

Shape is one lever. `semantic.radius.action` is the system's single shape value — interactive controls (buttons, inputs, badges, alerts, segmented items) all resolve to it, and Tailwind's `rounded-md` maps to it exactly so the utility and the token cannot disagree. Containers sit one step above at `rounded-lg` (`action + 4px`, and square when `role.radius` is 0); `rounded-sm` (`action - 2px`) is for chrome nested inside a control. `full` is reserved for pills and circular forms, and `0px` only for intentional outer canvas or substrate boundaries, never everyday UI controls. Reshaping the whole system means overriding `role.radius` in one tenant overlay — that is how `brutalist-demo` goes square in a single value.

<!-- auto:start:radius -->
| Tier | Value | Token | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Action | `8px` | `semantic.radius.action` | Buttons, inputs, badges, alerts, disclosures, segmented control items |
| Container | `12px` | `role.radius` + 4px (`rounded-lg`) | Cards, surfaces, segmented control surface, modal/sheet containers |
| Full | `9999px` | `primitive.radius.full` | Pills, avatars, indicator dots, any intentionally circular form |
| Zero | `0px` | `primitive.radius.0` | Outer canvas / substrate boundaries only — never on everyday UI controls |
| Scale sm | `8px` | `semantic.radius.scale.sm` (`rounded-scale-sm`) | chips, menu items and small surfaces. |
| Scale md | `12px` | `semantic.radius.scale.md` (`rounded-scale-md`) | cards, popovers and panels. |
| Scale lg | `16px` | `semantic.radius.scale.lg` (`rounded-scale-lg`) | dialogs, sheets and large media frames. |
| Scale xl | `24px` | `semantic.radius.scale.xl` (`rounded-scale-xl`) | hero media and feature panels. |
| Scale pill | `9999px` | `semantic.radius.scale.pill` (`rounded-scale-pill`) | pills, tags and avatar chips. |
<!-- auto:end:radius -->

## Elevation

Depth is communicated through 4 elevation roles bundled by `semantic.elevation.*`. Each role bundles a surface, shadow, and border so primitives can't mismatch them.

### Elevation roles

| Surface                                   | Role token                    | Background         | Shadow            | Border                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Card / panel resting                      | `semantic.elevation.flat`     | `surface.page`     | none              | none by default; opt-in 1px (`bordered`/`tone`/`accent`)        |
| Card / panel lifted (interactive only)    | `semantic.elevation.raised`   | `surface.raised`   | `shadow.subtle`   | none                                                            |
| Tooltip                                   | `semantic.elevation.floating` | `surface.inverse`  | `shadow.floating` | none                                                            |
| Menu / popover / listbox / toast / dialog | `semantic.elevation.overlay`  | `surface.floating` | `shadow.overlay`  | `border.default` 1px: the edge over `surface.muted` and in dark |

Cards default to `flat`. They lift to `raised` only on interactive hover or when explicitly elevated above siblings. Never combine `raised` with a border — depth is one mechanism (border OR shadow), not both stacked. The default `Card` variant is **borderless** (12d-3 outline rule: repeated outlined cards crowd a layout, so the edge is not the default) — a resting 1px border is **opt-in** via `bordered`, a feedback `tone`, or the `accent` variant (`border.default` / feedback color / `border.accent` respectively). Rely on whitespace, dividers, and rails for grouping; reach for `bordered` only for a genuinely discrete standalone object.

### Soft surfaces (ADR-064, hds#891)

Separate by **tone and space, not outlines**. Containers (Card, panels, Dialog, Menu, Popover, Select, Toast, CodeBlock, the Tabs list, the SegmentedControl track, Tag pills and chips) have no resting border: they sit on a surface step (`surface.page` → `raised` → `muted`/`overlay`). Borders stay only where they carry meaning: inputs, focus rings, selected or active states, feedback tones and the accent highlight, dense tables, Divider and the Kbd edge. The Table is the one outlined container (hds#1198): a 1px `border.default` frame with the container radius, a raised header, row dividers and no second line under the last row; its cells center their content vertically with equal top and bottom density padding. Controls are soft filled: the secondary Button is `surface.soft` with no border, and primary and secondary Buttons carry the **hard shadow** (zero blur, straight down on a fixed base: rest 3px, hover sinks 1px onto 2px, press sinks 3px onto 0px, so the button compresses and the bottom of the edge never moves; its colour is the button's own fill stepped darker in both themes, hds#897 and C2) and the directional **wipe** hover by default; opt out per button with `shadow="none"` / `hoverEffect="none"`. Kbd follows the same light source (2px). Each edge is precomputed as `--hds-edge-*` (override per component with `--hds-btn-edge` / `--hds-kbd-edge`); `semantic.color.shadow.hard` stays exported but is no longer the default.

Overlays (Dialog, AlertDialog, Menu, Popover, Select, Tooltip) portal into the nearest `data-hds` scope, so they inherit its theme (for example `<div data-hds data-theme="dark">`); pass `container` on the Content part to override.

## Motion

<!-- auto:start:motion -->
Motion (lift on hover, parallax) is the interaction-affordance layer; static depth comes from the `semantic.elevation.*` role-token bundles.

### Duration tiers

| Tier | Value | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primitive.duration.instant` | `100ms` | Immediate dismissals, binary toggles |
| `primitive.duration.short` | `150ms` | Productive micro-interactions (default for hover/focus/press) |
| `primitive.duration.medium` | `250ms` | Expressive entrances, teaching moments |
| `primitive.duration.long` | `400ms` | Spatial movement, page travel, parallax |

### Semantic intents

| Intent | Duration | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `semantic.motion.productive` | `150ms` | For micro-interactions and status changes. No deformation. |
| `semantic.motion.expressive` | `250ms` | For teaching moments and significant UI entries. Includes physics-based squish. |
| `semantic.motion.spatial` | `400ms` | For elements traveling long distances across the viewport. |
| `semantic.motion.exit` | `100ms` | For elements being removed from the DOM. |

Default most interactive feedback to `productive` (150ms, decelerate). Use `expressive` (250ms, spring) for entrances and moments where a little bounce adds delight. `spatial` (400ms) is for travel, not decoration.

### Other semantic motion tokens

| Token | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `semantic.motion.distance` | `24px` | Scroll-reveal translateY travel distance. Equals semantic.space.scale.md today, but names motion travel, not a spacing tier (hds#242). |
<!-- auto:end:motion -->

## Components

<!-- auto:start:components -->
| Component | Radius | States | Guidance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Buttons** (`Button`) | `8px` (`semantic.radius.action`) | default · hover · focus · active · disabled · loading | Three variants: primary (accent-filled), secondary (outline), tertiary (ghost). Primary uses `semantic.accent.*` ramp per state. Pressed is a 5% `semantic.color.state.pressed.overlay` wash over the fill (`role.pressed-overlay`: black in light, white in dark), not a brightness filter. Icon-only buttons (`iconOnly`) follow the same token surface. Icon-only actions use `Button iconOnly` with a `label` and an `Icon` from `@hirobius/design-system/icons` in `iconLeft`. |
| **Inputs** (`Input`) | `8px` (`semantic.radius.action`) | default · focus · filled · error · disabled · loading | Border-driven treatment; no filled background by default. Focus uses `semantic.color.border.accent` plus a 2px outline offset. Error swaps to `component.input.borderError`. |
| **Cards** (`Card`) | `12px` (`rounded-lg`, role radius + 4px) | default · hover (optional parallax) · pressed (when interactive) | Cards default to `elevation.flat` (borderless by default; an opt-in 1px border via `bordered`/`tone`/`accent`, no shadow). Interactive cards lift to `elevation.raised` (shadow.subtle, no border) on hover. Bind via `semantic.elevation.{role}` — never raw box-shadow values. Radius: `rounded-lg` (role radius + 4 px, follows the tenant knob) — never a hard-coded value. Padding: `var(--semantic-space-surface-padding)`. Title: `heading3`. Meta: `caption` + `var(--semantic-color-content-secondary)`. Hover (interactive): `scale(1.02)` transform + lift to raised. Never: gradients, glow, frosted glass, tinted surfaces, decorative overlays, or inner shadows. |
| **Badges** (`Badge`) | `8px` (`primitive.radius.4`) | neutral · accent · feedback (error/success/warning/info) | Single-line status markers. Feedback colors come from `semantic.color.feedback.*`. Never used as decorative chrome. |
| **Alerts** (`Alert`) | `8px` (via `hds.borderRadius.4`) | info · success · warning · error | Inline banner pattern with icon + message + optional action. Tone is carried by a tinted feedback fill (`bg-feedback-bg-*`, matching Badge), NOT a left-border stripe. Callout shares this fill language and differs only by role (no icon, no status role, optional italic). |
| **Disclosures** (`Disclosure`) | `8px` (`hds.borderRadius.action`) | collapsed · expanded · hover · focus | Accordion primitive. Expansion uses `semantic.motion.productive` by default; a spring is fine where it adds delight. Dividers follow `semantic.color.border.subtle`. |
| **Toggles** (`Toggle`) | `full` (pill track + circular thumb) | off · on · focus · disabled | Accent-filled track in the on state; neutral track otherwise. Track + thumb transitions share `semantic.motion.productive`. |
| **Segmented Control** (`SegmentedControl`) | Outer `12px` · inner segments `8px` | rest · hover · selected · disabled | Selected segment fills with the accent; unselected segments are transparent. Use for 2–5 mutually exclusive options; beyond that, prefer `Select`. |

See `public/hds-manifest.json` and `src/app/data/component-api.json` for the full inventory and prop tables.
<!-- auto:end:components -->

A tag input is a creatable Combobox (`<Combobox multiple creatable>`): chips inline in the field, suggestions as you type, Enter adds the typed value. Do not build a second chip-input component.

When a component or pattern needs visual inspiration, look at [21st.dev](https://21st.dev) first; it is inspiration only, so take ideas, never code (its gradients, glow and glass break the rules above), and HDS tokens and rules always win.

### Touch size (hds#750)

On a coarse pointer (any phone or tablet) or a viewport under 640px, small controls lift to `semantic.size.touchTarget` (`--semantic-size-touchTarget`, 44px): sm Button (icon-only sm in both axes), Tabs trigger, SegmentedControl option, Tag and its dismiss X, Disclosure trigger, Input clear, Combobox chips, Checkbox/Radio/Toggle rows and Pagination. It is on by default, with no prop; a fine pointer on a wide viewport keeps desktop density. A custom control opts in with the `hds-touch-row` class (height) or `hds-touch-target` (height and width). Hosts can delete their own touch-size overrides. `pnpm check:docs-touch-targets` measures the docs demos on a 390px phone and a 1024px touch tablet.

In the same query, text fields set their text at 16px (`--primitive-typography-size-base`) so iOS Safari does not zoom the page into a focused field: Input sm and md, Textarea, TokenField and the Combobox and CommandPalette search fields carry the `hds-touch-text` hook (Input lg is 18px already). A custom text field opts in with the same class. While Input's clear button shows, the end padding is 44px at every size, so typed text never runs under the grown button (hds#863).

### Card Anatomy (mandatory — all properties non-negotiable)

Every HDS card surface must conform to this anatomy exactly. No creative interpretation is permitted on any of these properties.

| Property                 | Required value                                                                                                                                                                            | Forbidden                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Background               | `var(--semantic-color-surface-raised)`                                                                                                                                                    | Any gradient, tinted fill, or custom color                                                  |
| Border                   | Default variant: **borderless**. Opt-in (`bordered`/`tone`/`accent`): 1px solid the matching token (`border.default` / feedback color / `border.accent`). Never border + shadow together. | `box-shadow` as an elevation substitute; a border on the default variant (use `bordered`)   |
| Border radius            | `rounded-lg` (`role.radius` + 4 px: 12 px by default, follows the direction or brand)                                                                                                     | `var(--component-card-radius)`, `rounded-full`, or any hard-coded value                     |
| Padding                  | `var(--semantic-space-surface-padding)` or `<HdsSurface padding="component">`                                                                                                             | Raw pixel values or ad hoc insets                                                           |
| Shadow                   | Resting cards: none (`elevation.flat`). Interactive lifted state: `shadow.subtle` via `elevation.raised`                                                                                  | Raw `box-shadow` values, `drop-shadow`, glow, or any depth effect not bound to a role token |
| Title                    | `hds.typeStyles.title` / `<Text variant="title">`                                                                                                                                         | Any other type style for the primary card heading                                           |
| Subtitle / meta          | `<Text variant="caption" tone="secondary">` (`hds.typeStyles.caption` + `semantic.color.content.secondary`)                                                                               | Primary content color or body size for secondary text                                       |
| Hover (interactive only) | `transform: scale(1.02)`                                                                                                                                                                  | Background fill change, border color shift, or opacity fade on hover                        |

An entity card (a job, a lead, a listing) fills four zones in this order: `Card.Source` (an `Avatar` size `sm`, the source name, a `Timestamp`), `Card.Header` with the `Card.Title`, `Card.Facts` (a wrapping caption row of 16px decorative icons with a text label each, rendered as a list), and the actions in `Card.Footer`. Facts are icon + text only; term and description pairs stay in `MetadataList`, and a text-only line stays in `MetaLine`. Status goes in the header `metadata` slot, never in the facts row.

**No cards within cards, ever (hds#1046).** A `Card` or section surface (`Surface`, `Callout`, or any raised or bordered wrapper) never contains another `Card` or surface. This covers the **section surface wrapping a card list**: a "Review new" section drawn as a card holding a list of job cards is wrong. Declare the group with type hierarchy instead (a section title, a count, surrounding metadata) on a plain region, and separate list items with spacing or dividers. `hds/no-nested-cards` (in `hds/recommended`) fails on it; list your own wrappers that draw a card or a surface in its `cards` / `surfaces` options.

Never use on any card surface: gradient backgrounds, glow effects, frosted glass (`backdrop-filter: blur`), decorative overlays, gradient borders, colored or tinted backgrounds, inner shadows, patterned fills, shimmer or noise effects.

## Screen Patterns

Five patterns sit above the primitives so that every screen is composed the same way. Import them from `@hirobius/design-system/patterns`.

### Page title rule

Every screen has exactly one `PageHeader`. The page title is `title` (28px), a fixed size with no size prop; `level` changes only the DOM heading element. `display` is reserved for marketing and landing surfaces and is never a screen title. Breadcrumb goes in the `breadcrumb` slot, facts (source, stage) as a `Badge` row in `metadata` above the title, the one state `Badge` in `status`, screen-level actions in `actions`.

### Which one, when

Pick by what the thing is. The first four rows are for a headline number or a state; the rest are for containers and sections.

| Component            | Use it for                                                                    | Use instead                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MetricTiles`        | The default for any row of headline numbers on a screen. One fixed tile size. | Nothing: start here.                                                         |
| `Stat`               | An inline number inside prose or a dense list.                                | `MetricTiles` when the number stands alone in a row of its own.              |
| `Card.Metric`        | A metric inside an existing `Card` only.                                      | `MetricTiles` when there is no enclosing `Card`.                             |
| `Card.Row`           | State with notes and a trailing badge, never a number (was `StatusTile`).     | `MetricTiles` when the tile is a number; a status row never carries a value. |
| `Card`               | A titled or interactive content object (header, body, footer, `selectable`).  | `Surface` when there is no title and nothing to press.                       |
| `Surface`            | A plain padded background around content that has no header of its own.       | `Card` when the content is titled or interactive.                            |
| `DestructiveSection` | The one irreversible action on a screen, with an explanation and a confirm.   | `FormActions` `destructive` slot for a delete beside a form's own buttons.   |
| `DataTableSection`   | A titled table with a toolbar, row actions and an empty state.                | `Table` alone when there is no heading, toolbar or empty state to show.      |

Three more needs are props on an existing component, not components of their own. A card people pick from a set is a `Card` with `selectable`, `selected` and `onSelectedChange`, announced as a checkbox. A wrapping row of equal tiles that are not headline numbers is a `Grid` with `layout="auto-fill"` and `minItemWidth`. A count beside a heading is a count `Badge`: `count`, `max` for a `99+` cap and a `label` such as "12 roles", in a `Stack direction="row" gap="xs"` with the heading. A state shown only as a colored marker, with no notes, is a `Badge` with `dot` and a `label` that names the state. An account button is an `Avatar` as the `iconLeft` of a `tertiary` `iconOnly` `Button` (`rounded-full`): initials when signed in, `fallback="icon"` when signed out, and `status="warning"` with a `statusLabel` while unsynced; the Button `label` names the account and its status. Never a hand-drawn icon in a bordered box. A rail that selects in place (master-detail, no routing) is `NavList` with `onSelect` and `selected` on each `NavList.Item`, a button marked `aria-current="true"`; a rail that routes keeps `href` and `current`. The two are exclusive. A second control on a rail row (a posting link, a row menu) is the item's `action`: it renders beside the row's link or button, never inside it. A button whose hover fill should slide in from the edge the pointer enters is a `Button` with `hoverEffect="wipe"` (opt-in, hover-capable pointers only, instant under reduced motion); never hand-roll a hover overlay. The `Kbd` key edge is `--semantic-shadow-key`, a 2px drop in `border.strong`; by default it is the same straight-down hard shadow as the Button (`0 2px 0`, colour `--hds-kbd-edge`, default its own fill stepped darker, `--hds-edge-kbd`).

`Card` and `Surface` share one container radius, `rounded-lg` (`role.radius` + 4 px: 12 px by default, 0 under `brutalist-demo`). Dialogs and alert dialogs use it too. Never read `--component-card-radius` for a container; it ignores the direction or brand.

`MetricTiles` has `min(tiles, 4)` columns, so a row never leaves an empty column, and every tile has one fixed min-height with the value in `title`, the label in `caption` and the sub line in `caption`. Its tone comes from the fixed feedback vocabulary: `neutral | success | warning | danger | info`.

A pager for one item at a time ("‹ 1 of 4 ›") is `Pagination` with `variant="compact"`; the default variant is for pages of a long result set.

### Destructive and table sections

`DestructiveSection` is a titled danger zone with one danger `Button` that opens an `AlertDialog`; it never runs the action from the button itself, only from the dialog's confirm. Put it last on the screen, below the form. `DataTableSection` puts a `Table` under a heading and a toolbar slot. Row actions are consumer nodes in a trailing column, an empty `rows` array shows an `EmptyState`, and the table scrolls horizontally inside the section on narrow widths, so a caller never sets `minWidth`.

### Form actions rule

`FormActions` puts the primary submit last in DOM order and right-most, with the secondary or cancel action immediately to its left. A destructive action goes on the far left, apart from the other two, and never to the right of the primary. The row is not sticky unless `sticky` is set.

An expandable list row (one-line preview, actions beside the trigger) is `Disclosure variant="row"`; do not build one from `Card.Row` plus custom state.

## Do's and Don'ts

- Don't invent new corner behavior for interactive controls; buttons, inputs, disclosures, and similar action surfaces should follow the shared action radius (`semantic.radius.action`).
- Don't introduce additional accent hues; Hirobius uses exactly one accent, resolved from `semantic.accent.rest`, over a near-monochrome, midnight-tinted neutral system. The accent is a knob each direction or brand sets (ADR-035) and defaults to a midnight graphite (`data-accent="cobalt"` swaps in cobalt) — read the token, never assume a hue.
- Don't add other tints to the neutrals; the only one is the faint midnight lean (OKLCH hue 262, hds#755), and greys stay high-contrast.
- Don't reach for shadow values directly — bind to a `semantic.elevation.*` role so surface + shadow + border stay paired.
- Don't transform text to uppercase anywhere; sentence case, per the Casing rule above.
- Don't paint status dots or coloured left accent bars on cards and tiles; status is implied by content. Don't put a heading over a card of supporting meta (a "Status" heading far from its "Applied" badge); keep label and value together.
- Don't hardcode colors, spacing, radius, or typography values when governed tokens already exist.
- Don't crowd the canvas; if a layout feels compressed, remove complexity before removing breathing room.
- Don't outline a container to group it; use a surface step or space (soft surfaces, ADR-064). Don't default repeated groups to outlined cards; prefer open bands, section dividers, accent rails, tabs, disclosures, and whitespace. Cards are for genuinely discrete repeated objects, not the primary layout language.
- Don't sticker badges onto the ends of prose lines. Status and progress should live in a predictable metadata slot, rail, header zone, table column, or progress surface; badges are reserved for compact state markers where their placement is intentional.
- Don't add decorative illustration, ornamental icons, or trend-driven filler that lacks functional or structural purpose.
- Don't ship motion that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`. Spring or expressive motion and a small press transform (such as a `whileTap` scale) are welcome where they add delight; under reduced motion, drop the transform and keep the color and state change.
- Don't define a global disabled-state rule (opacity multiplier, saturation ramp, etc.); disabled presentation is governed per-component through its dedicated disabled tokens.

## Open Questions

Unresolved rules that the live repo cannot yet answer confidently are tracked as GitHub issues. Do not invent rules here to fill those gaps.
